title: Line Fourteen

panels.scene: A soybean field in Ohio at dusk. An anonymous figure in a hard hat stands at a chain-link fence around a small substation; beside them a figure in a suit holds a folded term sheet and points at a transformer rather than at the half-built server hall on the horizon.
panels.dialogue: Show me the transformer. Skip the racks.

panels.scene: A bare conference room. A whiteboard where three boxes — chips, data center, power company — have been connected by arrows that curve back into each other, forming a closed loop. A junior analyst traces the loop with a marker, having run out of places for the arrow to end.
panels.caption: The circle closed, and everyone kept calling it a supply chain.

panels.scene: A public utility rate hearing in a municipal room: folding chairs, a paper easel listing service classes — residential, irrigation, grain dryers — and a clerk at a microphone reading from a tariff schedule. In the third row of chairs, among farmers and a bored reporter, sits a single unlabeled server rack, patiently waiting its turn.
panels.dialogue: Intelligence is a service class now. Line fourteen.

altText: A chip investor inspects a substation instead of servers, a whiteboard diagram of the deal loops back on itself, and at a utility rate hearing a lone server rack sits in the audience as intelligence is read out as tariff line fourteen.
sourceHeadline: Nvidia in talks to put $3B into the power company behind OpenAI's Ohio data center
